Wireframes v3 · as-built

Flyeasy, drawn from the code

Every screen below is transcribed from the current React Native source — routes from the expo-router tree, measurements from components/ui, colour and type straight out of theme/. The two typefaces are the app's own, embedded from node_modules, so the specimens set exactly as the build does.

01

Navigation map

Three stacked layers: a resolver at the root, an unauthenticated stack, and an authenticated tab bar with detail routes pushed on top. Both app/index.tsx and app/(app)/_layout.tsx redirect on session state, so the auth boundary is enforced twice.

Root resolver

app/_layout.tsx → app/index.tsx

AnimatedSplash → FontGate → AuthProvider → index · session? → yes → (app)/find → no → welcome screen

Unauthenticated

app/(auth)/

welcome → sign-up → confirm email → log-in ↔ forgot-password

Authenticated — tab bar

app/(app)/_layout.tsx · redirects to / when session is null

Find Flights Connect Chat Me

Pushed over the tabs

card presentation, except add-flight which is a modal

Find→user/[id] · Flights→flight/[id] →Find · Connect→chat/[id]
flight/add · modal · aboutcontact legal/termslegal/privacy delete-account

The core loop is Flights → flight detail → Find → connect → Connections → Chat. Find and Connections both scope their list to a flight chosen from the same FlightChips strip, so a flight is the unit of context everywhere people appear.

Mark — source vs. shipped

The mark above is ported from components/ui/Mark.tsx, which is what the app actually renders. Its plane geometry matches brand_designs/flyeasy-logo.svg exactly — the component's nested translates net out to the same origins — but the two have drifted on fold shading:

Foldflyeasy-logo.svgMark.tsx (shipped)Effect
Right plane#47723c#36532e The component computes darken(accent, 0.6) rather than reading the greenDark brand token — which exists and is commented "plane fold shadow". Ships noticeably darker.
Left plane#1f2420 @ 0.85#1f2420 @ 1.0 The source softens the fold; the component doesn't.

Deliberate on the right plane — the computed darken is what lets the fold follow a user-chosen accent, which a fixed token can't do. The left plane's missing opacity looks like an oversight. Worth reconciling if the logo is ever re-exported from the SVG.

06

Detail screens & modals

Pushed above the tab bar. Add-flight is the only true modal, and the only multi-step form in the app — it verifies against a live airline schedule rather than trusting typed input.

Activity suggestions — state machine

app/flight/[id].tsx → SuggestionsSection · lib/suggestions.ts

idle · "Suggest spots at JFK" — tap → loading · "Generating suggestions…" → loaded · result cards
on failure → error + Try again · switch Origin/Destination → back to idle

Every one of these states renders in place on the flight-detail page, in the slot the button occupied — none of them is a separate screen. The request carries the airport's IATA code, name, city, terminal, the direction, and hoursUntilFlight — computed from the scheduled departure, and null once the flight has left — so the model can weight a two-hour wait differently from a same-day connection.

Add flight — step machine

app/flight/add.tsx · lib/aerodatabox.ts → lookupFlight()

search — look up → 0 matches → inline error · exactly 1 → auto-picked · 2+ → pick
pick → confirm — save → (app)/flights · date popup · Modal

The lookup is not single-result. lookupFlight() returns an array: empty produces an inline error, exactly one skips the pick step and jumps straight to confirm, and two or more open the pick list. One result is the common case only because the request pins dateLocalRole=Departure — without it an overnight flight surfaces twice, once for the previous day's departure that lands on the searched date.

08

State coverage

Which screens handle which async states today. Every tab has a loading and empty state; error states with a retry action are the gap — three screens still fail silently or fall back to stale content.

ScreenLoadingEmptyError + retryNotes
find Spinner 4 variants Try again Best-covered screen
flights Spinner No flights / no matches Try again Distinguishes empty from filtered-empty
connections Spinner Per tab Try again Chat-thread fetch fails silently by design
chat Spinner No chats yet Silent Keeps prior threads on failure
me — — Native alerts Reads session from context
flight/[id] Spinner Flight not found Suggestions only Traveler fetch fails silently
flight/add Button spinner No matches Inline ErrorText Three-step form
chat/[id] Spinner Say hello Native alert Paused is a first-class state
user/[id] Spinner No shared flights Silent —

Cross-cutting patterns

Four conventions recur across the screens above and are worth holding to in anything new:

PatternRule
Destructive actions confirmWithdraw, delete flight and delete account all interrupt with a native alert or typed confirmation. Accept and Connect do not.
Unavailable dims, never hidesA paused person stays listed at 55% opacity. Only the content dims — the action pills stay at full strength so they don't read as disabled.
Empty states name the cause"You've paused connecting" and "You're all connected" are separate from "You're first!" — the screen never implies a flight is empty when it isn't.
Fill encodes pressabilitySolid or tinted means actionable; outlined means status. The one exception, requested, earns a trailing ✕ to signal it can still be pressed.

How this was made. Screens transcribed from the route tree at 25db7b2 on design-changes. Colour values are copied from theme/palettes.ts, measurements from components/ui, and both typefaces are embedded from the same @expo-google-fonts packages the app loads at runtime — so type here sets as it does on device.

Fidelity notes. Icons are the real Ionicons glyphs, embedded from @expo/vector-icons and referenced by the exact names the source passes — so chatbubble here is the same mark the tab bar renders. Phone frames are a flat 320×680 with no device chrome or safe-area insets. Screens are drawn at the shipped defaults — green accent, warm background — and long lists are truncated to fit one screen height. The welcome screen's logo is <Mark> itself, its path geometry and transforms copied from components/ui/Mark.tsx; only the splash wave animation is omitted.

Supersedes _design/Flyeasy Wireframes v2.html (13 July 2026), which predates the move to Bricolage Grotesque and does not include the chat, connections, suggestions or account-deletion flows.
